newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end bourse trade sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: German shares end bourse trade sharply lower.

text.p: German equities ended bourse trade in Frankfurt on Tuesday sharply lower, driven down by negative sentiment after a U.S. missile attack on Iraqi air defence targets.

The markets were also anxiously awaiting U.S. economic data later in the day. With the U.S. markets closed on Monday for the Labor Day holiday and an absence of corporate data at home, German markets were desperately seeking new impetus to boost trade.

At the end of bourse trade the DAX index, which measures trade in Germany's 30 largest shares was down 22.11 points, or 0.87 percent, at 2,510.77 points. Weaker German debt did not help the market's mood.
The news that the U.S. had launched missile attacks on Iraqi air defence targets lifted the dollar by half a pfennig against the mark.
However, the higher dollar did little to boost chemical stocks, the expected reaction to a stronger U.S. currency.
BASF AG was down 63 pfennigs at 43.15 marks, while Hoechst AG was down 63 pfennigs at 50.85 marks and Bayer AG was down 40 pfennigs at 52.05 marks.
Deutsche Bank was lower on newspaper reports that funds had been suspended at its Deutsche Morgan Grenfell unit.
Deutsche was down 62 pfennigs at 72.25 marks at the end of bourse trade.
